construction_notes: Page numbers in this extraction are the printed journal pages 869-902 (PDF page + 868).

Grades are on the scale 0, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13; graduates need a GPA of at least 6, so recorded GPAs range from 6 to 13; the GPA is standardized for the regressions, and the overall standard deviation of grades is 1.
Discrete treatment variable: one for students in municipalities with below median iodine concentration in drinking water.

Continuous treatment variable: Treat = -log(IodineConcentration), scaled so that the difference between the 95th and 5th percentiles equals one, so coefficients reflect going from the 95th to the 5th percentile.

Iodine concentration in drinking water ranges from 1 to 67 ug per liter across municipalities and is built from 2,800 GEUS groundwater samples matched to water works (five nearest) and collapsed to municipality level.
Predicted urinary iodine from IodineUrine = 43.2 + 1.7 * IodineWater (Pedersen et al., 1999), converted to ug per liter assuming 1.5 litres of average daily urine output.

Parental control variables are measured eight years prior to graduation to avoid bad controls; all control variables are discretized and entered as dummies, with dummies for missing values (unknown or dead parent).
Wealth and income variables in Table 1 are converted to 2011 levels using nominal GDP.

Post-reform periods: P1 covers graduation years 1999-2001 and P2 graduation years from 2002, because the June 1998 and July 2000-April 2001 reforms came too late in the year to affect the 1998 and 2000/2001 graduating classes.
Standard errors are clustered at the level of treatment (municipality); Figure 5's quantile estimates use misspecification-robust standard errors instead.
Severe, moderate and mild iodine deficiency are defined as urinary iodine below 20, 20-50 and 50-100 ug per liter (Andersson et al., 2012).

key_assumptions.assumption: No causal interpretation is attached: the pre-reform difference is reported as a balance check, and the author notes that treatment assignment is not random but not systematically related to student characteristics
key_assumptions.supported_by: the author's own reading of Table 1, including the within-region re-estimation in column 4

threats_discussed: the treatment group is more likely to live in thinly populated (rural) areas and has lower parental wealth and income than the control group
robustness_checks: re-estimating the differences controlling for a West Denmark dummy (column 4)

estimator.value: OLS regression of the characteristic on the discrete treatment variable

estimation.specification: Regression of pre-reform GPA on the discrete treatment variable, controlling for a West Denmark dummy so that the coefficient reflects within-region differences

heterogeneity.finding: In column 3 the only statistically significant differences are the share of boys (-0.014, p < 0.1) and the number of siblings (0.117, p < 0.01); in column 4 the coefficients are either insignificant or have the opposite sign to the raw differences in column 3.
